# Plan: Start/stop a system from the dashboard flow tab

## Goal

From the dashboard's Flow tab, start and stop a scaffolded system — i.e. run the
system host (`dotnet run --project <systemDir>/<name>-host`) — with visible
status and logs. Local developer convenience only; nothing touches git, GitOps,
or any cluster.

## Context and constraints (verified against the codebase)

- `internal/dashboard/server.go` package doc currently states: *"It starts no
  integration processes and changes nothing."* This feature deliberately breaks
  that invariant for the local-runtime case; the doc and the `dashboard`
  command's `Long:` help text (`cmd/intropy/dashboard.go`) must be updated.
  The doc's other principle — commands own the refusals that matter — applies
  to facts derived from git/ArgoCD and does not bind here: process state is
  local, ephemeral runtime state with no command-line truth to contradict.
- No new CLI verb. AGENTS.md's closed verb vocabulary (read-only /
  project-state / move-publish) has no home for process supervision, and a CLI
  is the wrong shape for it anyway (short-lived process supervising a
  long-lived one). The lifecycle machinery goes in an internal package the
  dashboard calls as a library, mirroring how `systems.go` calls
  `system.Create`/`system.Update`. If a terminal use case proves real later,
  a verb can wrap the same package then.
- **Routing constraint (verified experimentally with Go 1.26):** net/http
  ServeMux panics at registration if a `{path...}` wildcard is not the last
  segment. Therefore `POST /api/systems/{path...}/run` is impossible.
  Consequences:
  - Run endpoints get their own prefix: `GET|POST|DELETE /api/run/{path...}`.
  - Verified: `/api/run/acme/billing` matches; `/api/run` (empty wildcard)
    does not match — the workspace-root system (identifier `.`) must be
    addressed explicitly as `/api/run/.`. Existing `byPath` already treats
    empty as `.`, but with a dedicated prefix the browser-stripping problem
    doesn't arise the same way; still normalize `""`→`.` defensively in the
    handler for consistency.
- Existing patterns to mirror:
  - Provider/mutex caching bargain: `topoMu`, `depMu` in `handlers.go`.
  - System dir resolution + host discovery: `resolveSystemDir` +
    `template.ListSystemHosts` (used by `systems.go` and `topology.go`).
  - Process execution with context + output tailing: `internal/topology/graph.go`
    (`RunGraph`, `tail`).
  - Flow tab already computes `sysDir` and `hasHost` (FlowView.tsx ~L298-299)
    and already POSTs to a system endpoint (`syncSystem`, api.ts ~L432) —
    the UI affordance pattern exists.

## Design

### Backend: new file `internal/dashboard/run.go`

Keep it in the dashboard package (not a new internal package) for v1: it is
only consumed by the dashboard, and `server.go`'s doc already concedes the
package runs subprocesses on request. Export nothing new; handlers hang off
`apiServer` like the rest. (If a CLI verb ever appears, extraction is trivial.)

**State on `apiServer`:**

```go
runMu sync.Mutex
runs  map[string]*systemRun // keyed by root-relative system dir
```

```go
type systemRun struct {
    cmd       *exec.Cmd
    startedAt time.Time
    // ring buffer of combined stdout/stderr lines
    logs  []string
    logMu sync.Mutex
    err   error // non-nil once the process has exited on its own
}
```

**Endpoints** (wired in `newHandler`, handlers.go):

- `POST /api/run/{path...}` — start. Resolve dir via `resolveSystemDir`, find
  the host via `template.ListSystemHosts(dir)` (422 if none: "no system host"),
  409 if already running. Launch:
  `dotnet run --project <hostDir>` (NOT `--no-build`: the developer just edited
  code; they want a build — unlike `RunGraph`, which builds separately only to
  keep stdout clean for JSON). Set `cmd.Dir = hostDir`? No — leave cwd unset;
  `--project` is explicit and the dashboard's cwd is the workspace root.
  Process must outlive the request: do NOT use `r.Context()`; use a context
  derived from the dashboard lifetime (plumb `Serve`'s ctx into `newHandler`,
  or store a cancel func on `apiServer` and cancel from `Serve`'s shutdown
  path — prefer the latter: `newHandler` signature stays unchanged, and
  `Serve` already owns the graceful shutdown select).
- `DELETE /api/run/{path...}` — stop. SIGTERM the process group, wait with a
  timeout (say 5s), then SIGKILL. 404 if not running.
- `GET /api/run/{path...}` — status: `{ running, pid, startedAt, uptimeSeconds,
  exitError? }`. Include the last N log lines (e.g. 200) so the UI can render
  them without a separate endpoint. Keep it a single GET — polling-friendly.

**Process-group kill (the known pitfall):** `dotnet run` spawns the actual host
as a child; killing only the dotnet process orphans the app holding its ports.
Use `SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` at start and `syscall.Kill(-pgid, sig)` to
stop. This is Unix-only — put the two calls behind a small file-pair
(`runproc_unix.go` with `//go:build !windows`, `runproc_windows.go` using
`taskkill /T` or CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP + GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent is
genuinely painful on Windows; acceptable v1: `cmd.Process.Kill()` only, with a
comment documenting the orphan risk). Match whatever the repo already assumes:
grep shows no existing Setpgid use, so this is the first platform-specific
code — keep it minimal and isolated.

**Log capture:** pipe stdout+stderr into one `io.Writer` that appends lines to
a bounded ring buffer (e.g. 1000 lines) under `logMu`. Needed because without a
terminal, the flow tab is the only place to see a failed start (missing
connection string, port in use, build error).

**Crash detection:** a goroutine per started run does `cmd.Wait()` and records
the exit error into `systemRun.err`, removing the entry from `runs` only on
*clean* stop via DELETE — an unexpected exit must keep the entry so GET can
report `{running: false, exitError: "..."}` and the UI can show the logs.

**Shutdown:** on `Serve` ctx cancellation, after `srv.Shutdown`, iterate `runs`
and SIGTERM-then-KILL each (same helper as DELETE). Child processes must not
outlive the dashboard.

**Concurrency:** one mutex (`runMu`) guards the map; per-run state has its own
`logMu`. Double-start is a 409, not a race. No serialization needed across
different systems — starting two systems concurrently is legitimate.

**Timeouts:** none on the run itself (that's the point of a long-lived dev
process). The 5s SIGTERM grace in stop is the only timeout.

**Dapr:** out of scope for v1. Plain `dotnet run`. Comment in code noting the
follow-up (sidecars, `local/dapr-components` wiring).

### API client: `web/src/api.ts`

Add types `RunState { running, pid?, startedAt?, exitError?, logs: string[] }`
and calls:

```ts
runState: (path: string) => getJSON<RunState>(`/api/run/${path}`),
startSystem: (path: string) => requestJSON<RunState>(`/api/run/${path}`, { method: 'POST' }),
stopSystem: (path: string) => requestJSON<RunState>(`/api/run/${path}`, { method: 'DELETE' }),
```

### Frontend: `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`

- In the header row next to the existing sync-host button (~L390), add
  Start/Stop, gated on the already-computed `hasHost` (no host → disabled with
  the same affordance style as the sync button's "no host" state).
- Poll `runState(sysDir)` while the system row is selected: every ~2s while
  running, once on selection otherwise. Stop polling on unmount/system switch
  (the file already resets per-system state in a `useEffect` keyed on
  `system`).
- Render status inline in the header (small dot + "running since …" / error
  text), and logs in a collapsible panel below the canvas (or reuse the
  FlowDetail drawer if a node is selected — simpler: a dedicated collapsible
  section, monospace, auto-scroll to bottom).
- Errors from POST/DELETE surface in the existing `syncError`-style banner
  pattern (add a parallel `runError` state or generalize).

### Docs/comments to update

- `internal/dashboard/server.go` package doc: the "starts no integration
  processes" sentence; reword to state the one exception (user-initiated
  local runs from the flow view) and that nothing else changed (still no git,
  no network beyond the existing providers).
- `cmd/intropy/dashboard.go` `Long:` text: currently says the dashboard "does
  not start any integration processes" — now false. Keep under the 150-word
  house limit; one clause: the flow view can start and stop a system's host
  locally.
- AGENTS.md: untouched (no new verb).

## Testing

- `internal/dashboard/run_test.go`: handler-level tests using a fake host.
  Can't run dotnet in tests — so put the exec behind a tiny seam: a
  `startFunc` field on apiServer (default real impl) or an interface
  `runner { Start(ctx, dir) (handle, error) }`. Prefer the function field;
  the package already injects providers as function values (`providers`
  struct) — follow that. Test: start→status→stop happy path, double-start
  409, stop-when-not-running 404, start without host 422, crash reported via
  GET, logs captured, shutdown kills children.
- Process-group behavior: unit-testable only on Unix; keep the platform files
  thin enough to review by eye. Add a manual test note in the PR description
  (start a real scaffolded system, stop it, verify port freed).
- Frontend: no test infra exists for the SPA (no test runner in package.json);
  verify manually per the repo's apparent convention.
- Run `make` (or the repo's lint/test targets) before PR — CONTRIBUTING.md
  governs.

## Explicitly out of scope

- New CLI verb (`sys run`/`stop`/`logs`) — rejected; see Context.
- Dapr sidecars, per-component start, dependency ordering.
- Restart, log streaming (SSE/websocket), build-on-change watching.
- Anything remote/cluster-side.

## Open questions for review

1. Log tail embedded in GET status vs separate endpoint — embedded chosen for
   polling simplicity; is 200 lines/response acceptable?
2. Workspace-root system addressing: `/api/run/.` — acceptable, or should the
   UI special-case the pseudo-system?
3. Windows support: is Unix-only process-group kill acceptable for v1 given
   the team is macOS-based (verify repo assumptions)?
4. Should stopping be refused (409) if the dashboard did not start the run
   (e.g. state lost)? v1: no — all runs are dashboard-started by construction.

content.text:
All claims checked. I verified the routing behavior experimentally against Go 1.26 (the repo's toolchain), read every file the plan cites, and confirmed the line references. Verdict and findings below.

---

## Verdict: **approve-with-changes**

The plan is well-grounded: the ServeMux panic claim, the `/api/run/{path...}` prefix workaround, the line references (FlowView.tsx L298–299, api.ts L431–432), the doc quotes in `server.go` and `dashboard.go`, the provider/mutex conventions, and the "no Setpgid in repo" claim all check out. The design fits the package's existing bargains. The findings below are mostly precision fixes and a few unhandled states, not redesigns.

## Findings

**1. [must-fix] The `/api/run/.` claim is experimentally wrong — and the "defensive" normalization is actually load-bearing.** I ran the exact patterns against Go 1.26's ServeMux: `/api/run/.` never reaches the handler with `path="."`. ServeMux cleans the path and 307-redirects to `/api/run/`, where the wildcard arrives as `""`. The plan's framing — "must be addressed explicitly as `/api/run/.`" plus "normalize `""`→`.` defensively" — inverts reality: `""`→`.` normalization is *mandatory*, and open question #2's premise dissolves. Same outcome as the existing `byPath` comment describes for `/api/integrations/`. The design lands correctly anyway; the plan text should state it plainly, and the handler must treat `""`, `/`, and `.` identically (mirroring `byPath`'s `Trim(..., "/")` then empty→`.`).

**2. [must-fix] The shutdown-plumbing proposal is internally inconsistent.** The plan says: "store a cancel func on `apiServer` and cancel from `Serve`'s shutdown path — `newHandler` signature stays unchanged." But `newHandler` returns `http.Handler`; `Serve` (server.go) holds only that interface and cannot reach the `apiServer` to cancel anything. One of the two has to give: either `newHandler` also returns the `*apiServer` (or a `shutdownRuns func()`), or the run state lives somewhere `Serve` owns. Pick one and write it into the plan; tests will need the same handle.

**3. [must-fix] Specify the post-crash state machine explicitly — as written it has a hole.** The plan says a crashed run *keeps* its map entry, POST returns "409 if already running," DELETE returns "404 if not running." Literal reading: after a crash, the entry exists with `running: false` — is POST a 409 (entry exists) or a restart (not running)? Is DELETE a 404, or does it clear the entry? The natural contract: POST restarts when `running == false` (replacing the entry), DELETE on a crashed entry clears it and returns 200, 404 only when no entry exists. Decide and add the two test cases (restart-after-crash, delete-after-crash); the current test list has "crash reported via GET" but neither transition out of the crashed state.

**4. [suggestion] The sync-vs-run race is unaddressed.** The flow tab's Start button will sit next to `syncHost`, and `syncSystem` rewrites host source files under `createMu`. `dotnet run` builds at start — starting a run while a sync is mid-rewrite yields a build against torn files. Cheap fix: take `createMu` (or a shared `hostMu`) briefly at run start, or document the accepted risk. Given the buttons are adjacent in the same toolbar, the collision is plausible, not theoretical.

**5. [suggestion] The "cwd is the workspace root" claim is wrong; the conclusion survives, but state the real invariant.** `Serve` resolves `root` to absolute, so `resolveSystemDir` returns an absolute `--project` path regardless of the dashboard process's cwd. Fine. But note `dotnet run --project X` runs with the project directory as working directory and applies the default launchSettings profile — whereas `RunGraph` deliberately passes `--no-launch-profile`. For a dev server the launch profile is probably *desired* (ports, environment); say so explicitly in the plan rather than leaving it to chance.

**6. [suggestion] Dapr deferral is a functional risk, not just a scope cut.** Integrations here scaffold `local/dapr-components` (handlers.go reads them), so a host that wires Dapr at startup may fail under plain `dotnet run` — precisely the failed-start case the log panel exists to show, but it would mean the feature doesn't work for real systems. Before the PR, verify a freshly scaffolded host actually boots without sidecars; if it doesn't, v1 needs `dapr run` or the feature ships broken. Keep the code comment, but make "verified a real scaffolded host starts standalone" a PR gate alongside the manual port-freed test.

**7. [suggestion] Minor placement inaccuracy in the frontend section.** The sync-host button lives in the *ghosts banner* (~L385–405), not the header toolbar (the toolbar holds only the picker and Refresh). The Start/Stop button's gating on `hasHost` is right, but "next to the existing sync-host button" should say where it actually goes — the toolbar is the better home anyway since it must be visible when there are no ghosts.

**8. [suggestion] Two small omissions in failure modes.** (a) A DELETE that races a natural exit should be idempotent-ish (404 with the exit error in the body is fine — just pick one). (b) If the dashboard itself is SIGKILLed, `Setpgid` children are orphaned holding their ports; a one-line comment in `run.go` acknowledging this beats discovering it. Neither blocks approval.

**9. [suggestion] Conventions fit is good — two nits to keep it that way.** The test seam (`startFunc` function field) correctly mirrors the `providers` struct; the no-new-verb reasoning correctly applies AGENTS.md's closed vocabulary; the `Long:` rewrite must stay under the 150-word ceiling (current text is ~60 words, plenty of room). One addition: per AGENTS.md, error strings from the new endpoints should front-load what failed (`system already running: acme/billing`, not `cannot start because…`) — the plan lists status codes but not message shapes.

Nothing here is over-scoped — the exclusions (SSE, restart, per-component start, remote) are all correct cuts. With findings 1–3 folded in, I'd approve the plan as-is.
